status.statement: Engineering evidence prepared by a tool; not a subject review. An engineering agent cannot sign this packet.

taskIntent.purpose: Predict, then observe, how the step size η and the curvature a determine the positions produced by fixed-step gradient descent on f(x) = a·x²/2.

stages.instruction: Before any iterations are shown, predict what the positions x_n will do over the first few updates for the three comparison step sizes η = 0.25, 0.75 and 1.25 (curvature a = 2, start x₀ = 4).

response.prompt: For η = 0.25, 0.75 and 1.25 with a = 2 and x₀ = 4, what do you expect the positions to do over the first few iterations, and why?

stages.instruction: Change the step size η and step through the iterations one at a time. Use the scenarios to compare η = 0.25, 0.75 and 1.25, and compare what you see with your prediction.
Now change the curvature a as well as the step size. Notice how the step sizes that give each kind of behaviour change with a.
Explain in your own words how the step size and the curvature together determine what the positions do.

response.prompt: How do η and a together determine whether the positions shrink, change sign, keep the same size or grow?

stages.instruction: Explore freely: change the step size, curvature and starting position, step through the iterations and compare the scenarios.

taskFamilies.description: Host-owned prediction request about how the step size changes fixed-step gradient descent on f(x) = a·x²/2. The host owns the response, its capture and any evaluation.
Host-owned explanation request about how step size and curvature together determine the iterates. The host owns the response, its capture and any evaluation.
Host-owned later task with a new curvature or a recurrence representation. Its prompts, held-out items and scoring stay with the host and are not part of this catalogue.

derivation.citation: Closed form written for this catalogue: f′(x) = a·x, so x_{n+1} = x_n − η·f′(x_n) = (1 − η·a)·x_n and, by induction, x_n = x0·(1 − η·a)^n. For x0 ≠ 0 the positions tend to 0 exactly when |1 − η·a| < 1, that is 0 < η·a < 2. Not independently reviewed.

Study Harness Original Project Specification (25 October 2026), section 10: exact quadratic gradient-descent worked example, boundary cases and staged controls, as carried into the Study Harness visualizer implementation report §12.3.

assumptions: The objective is exactly the quadratic f(x) = a·x²/2 with a > 0: no noise and no higher-order terms.
The step size η is the same for every update.

Evaluation is deterministic on every conforming JavaScript engine: values come from exactly specified arithmetic rounded once (a logarithm only estimates the first index of a numerical limit, which is then verified exactly), so the same parameters and iteration always give the same values.
Real numbers are IEEE-754 double-precision values; the product η·a is computed once in double precision and the regime is classified from it.
limitations: Positions are evaluated from the closed form x_n = x0·(1 − η·a)^n with extended-precision intermediates and one final rounding; the recurrence is not stepped.
Iterations are bounded to 0 ≤ n ≤ 1000, and η·a is at most 4.

Values beyond the double range are numerical-limit statuses: overflow above Number.MAX_VALUE with the last finite iteration, or underflow of a nonzero value to zero. Subnormal values are reported as reduced-precision approximations.
Displayed rounding is separate from computation: a value shown as 0 at display precision is not exact convergence, and the regime never depends on displayed digits.
The objective curve is sampled at 201 points; the polyline between samples does not certify values between them.

conventions.coordinate: Position x lies on a horizontal axis, positive to the right, with the minimum of f at x = 0. The iteration index n counts updates from n = 0; it is not a time.

a.label: Curvature
a.description: Curvature (second derivative) of the objective f(x) = a·x²/2. It must be positive.

eta.label: Step size
eta.description: Fixed step size multiplying the gradient in every update. A step size of 0 leaves the position unchanged.

start.position.label: Starting position
start.position.meaning: Position at iteration 0; equal to the parameter x0.
start.position.signConvention: Positive positions lie to the right of the minimum at x = 0.

start.loss.label: Starting loss
start.loss.meaning: Objective value a·x0²/2 at the starting position; never negative.

position.label: Position
position.meaning: Position after n fixed-step gradient-descent updates: x_n = x0·(1 − η·a)^n.
position.signConvention: Positive positions lie to the right of the minimum at x = 0.

loss.label: Loss
loss.meaning: Objective value a·x_n²/2 at the current position; never negative.

gradient.label: Gradient
gradient.meaning: Derivative a·x_n of the objective at the current position.
gradient.signConvention: Positive when the objective increases to the right.

multiplier.label: Update multiplier
multiplier.meaning: Factor r = 1 − η·a applied to the position by every update, using the double-precision product η·a.

product.label: Step size times curvature
product.meaning: Product η·a, computed once in IEEE-754 double precision; the regime is classified from this value.

threshold.label: Largest convergent step size
threshold.meaning: Step size 2/a. Positive step sizes below it bring a nonzero start to 0; at it the positions alternate with constant magnitude.

regime.label: Regime
regime.meaning: Classification from the declared conditions on x0 and the product p = η·a: zero-start (x0 = 0), stationary (p = 0), monotone-convergence (0 < p < 1), one-step (p = 1), alternating-convergence (1 < p < 2), oscillation (p = 2), divergence (p > 2). Never derived from iterates or displayed digits.

index.label: Iteration
index.meaning: Integer number of updates applied, from 0 to 1000. Not a time.

constraints.message: The step size times the curvature (η·a) can be at most 4, which keeps the update factor 1 − η·a at or above −3 and the iterations inside the supported numerical range.
constraints.recovery: Reduce the step size η or the curvature a until η·a is at most 4.

suite.author: Reference cases from the implementation report §12.3 plus cases derived by exact rational arithmetic in tests/reference/oracles/quadratic.ts, which shares no code with the catalogue kernel.
suite.review: No independent human subject reviewer has approved these cases. Automated agreement is engineering evidence only.

derivedFrom.conversion: Converted by explorable-models activity tooling: case IDs, labels, provenance, parameters and tolerances copied unchanged; quantity expectations restated as explorable-models.reference-fixtures 1.0 expectations. Parameter-only quantities restated at every point of a case: start.position is the case's x0 (declared equal to it), start.loss is the case's own loss expectation at n = 0, and product is the IEEE-754 double product of the case's η and a, which the suite's declared semantics define as p (compared exactly).

notCovered: Trace geometry (the trace ends at the current position or stops with a reason), the starting marker, the sampled objective curve and the current-iterate marker are checked by tests/reference/activities/quadratic.test.ts.

stages.instruction: Before any iterations are shown, predict what the positions x_n will do over the first few updates for the three comparison step sizes η = 0.25, 0.75 and 1.25 (curvature a = 2, start x₀ = 4).

response.prompt: For η = 0.25, 0.75 and 1.25 with a = 2 and x₀ = 4, what do you expect the positions to do over the first few iterations, and why?

stages.instruction: Change the step size η and step through the iterations one at a time. Use the scenarios to compare η = 0.25, 0.75 and 1.25, and compare what you see with your prediction.
Now change the curvature a as well as the step size. Notice how the step sizes that give each kind of behaviour change with a.
Explain in your own words how the step size and the curvature together determine what the positions do.

response.prompt: How do η and a together determine whether the positions shrink, change sign, keep the same size or grow?
